title: Clean and lubricate the motorcycle chain

steps.instruction: Raise the rear wheel on the paddock stand.
expert_tips: Use a paddock stand so you can get the back wheel on this bike up in the air
Disposable gloves to keep the gunk off my hands
Sunglasses to keep it out of my eyes
steps.check_hint: Rear wheel raised off the ground on the paddock stand

steps.instruction: Spray cleaner on one chain section and scrub.
expert_tips: We are cleaning off the old lube, which turns detritus into a grinding paste which can prematurely wear the chain
Clean a portion of the chain at one time rather than spraying the whole thing and having the cleaner dry out
The chain brush gets all three sides in one scrub, so you get all three sides in one scrub
Look for the brush marks to tell you have been all the way around the circuit of the chain
steps.check_hint: Whole chain has been sprayed and scrubbed, with brush marks visible around its circuit

steps.instruction: Rinse all the gunk off with water.
expert_tips: People who douse it with chain cleaner until the chain is shiny get through chain cleaner really, really quickly
I tend to use a garden hose, or a pump-up garden sprayer, to clean away any residue of gunk
steps.check_hint: Chain and sprocket rinsed, with water washing residue and gunk away

steps.instruction: Dry the chain by rolling through a rag.
expert_tips: Use a microfibre cloth or any old rag, try not one that's going to leave bits in your chain
On that bottom run, roll the chain through and try and get as much moisture out of there as you can
warnings: Be careful not to get fingers and stuff jammed in there
Definitely don't do this with the engine running
Try not to get fingers jammed in the teeth
steps.check_hint: Chain on the bottom run looks dry after passing through the rag

steps.instruction: Wipe the wheel rim and sprocket clean.
expert_tips: Gunk flung onto the back wheel and sprocket will be really stubborn to get rid of when you come to clean the bike
Bike cleaner is probably unlikely to get rid of it as well as that chain cleaner
Spray a bit of chain cleaner on the rag and use that rag to clean the wheel down
steps.check_hint: Wheel rim and sprocket wiped free of chain lube residue

steps.instruction: Ride briefly to dry and warm the chain.
expert_tips: This stage is more of an ideal world stage, to make sure there's absolutely no water left in the chain and just to get it warmed up
If you don't take it out, just make sure it's completely dry before you move on to the lubrication stage
steps.check_hint: Chain completely dry and warmed after the short ride

steps.instruction: Spray lube between sprocket, rollers and plates.
expert_tips: With a sealed chain, the job of the lube is just to avoid corrosion and protect it from rust
We just need a coating on the outer plates, on the rollers, and a bit between the chain and the sprockets
Give the chain lube a good shake and fit the straw into the nozzle, we don't want it to spray everywhere
First place I always put it is between the sprocket and the chain
Light, controlled spray on the outer plates, don't want to get loads, a couple of spins should be enough
steps.check_hint: Chain rollers and outer and inner plates evenly coated with lube

steps.instruction: Spin the rear wheel and leave bike standing.
expert_tips: Spin the back wheel a few times to try and get that lube to work through
Leave the bike to stand for a bit, let that solvent in the chain lube go off, and hopefully it will stay in place for your next ride
steps.check_hint: Lubed chain keeps its coating after the rear wheel is spun
